title: Towards Interpretable Depression Detection: Linking Acoustic Features to DSM-5 Indicators
abstract: arXiv:2608.26148v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Depression affects millions worldwide, yet diagnosis relies on subjective self-reports that may miss authentic behavior. This paper presents an approach linking speech acoustics to DSM-5 depressive-behavior indicators through a transparent Linkage Framework. Unlike black-box models, the framework explicitly maps acoustic features (pitch variability, pauses, speech tempo) to clinical indicators, enabling interpretable, indicator-level outputs. The system runs locally on commodity hardware (HW) to preserve privacy. Preliminary evaluation on DAIC-WOZ shows directionally consistent associations between acoustic features and DSM-5 indicators for psychomotor change and concentration difficulty, supporting the design rationale. Future work will validate on longitudinal datasets and extend multimodal integration while maintaining edge constraints.

translated_title: 面向可解释的抑郁症检测：将声学特征与DSM-5指标关联起来
translated_abstract: 抑郁症影响着全球数百万人，然而诊断依赖于可能错过真实行为的主观自我报告。本文提出了一种方法，通过透明的关联框架，将语音声学与DSM-5抑郁行为指标联系起来。与黑箱模型不同，该框架明确地将声学特征（如音高变异性、停顿、语速）映射到临床指标上，从而实现可解释的、基于指标级别的输出。系统在普通硬件上本地运行以保护隐私。在DAIC-WOZ上的初步评估显示，声学特征与DSM-5中精神运动变化和注意力困难指标之间存在方向一致的关联，支持了设计原理。未来工作将在纵向数据集上验证，并在保持边缘约束的同时扩展多模态集成。
tldr: 本文提出一种可解释的抑郁症检测框架，通过透明映射声学特征到DSM-5临床指标，在普通硬件上本地运行以保护隐私，初步验证了其有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an interpretable depression detection framework that transparently maps acoustic features to DSM-5 clinical indicators, runs locally on commodity hardware for privacy, and shows initial validation of its design.
